result.title: Depth Anyviewpoint? Evaluating Monocular Depth Over Viewpoint Sequences
result.summary: Monocular depth estimation aims to predict depth maps from single RGB images (forgoing the need for stereo camera pairs) and has seen impressive leaps in performance in recent work due to the introduction of affine-invariant losses and the use of foundation model features. These monocular depth models predict affine-invariant depth, which describes the relative positions of objects in the scene instead of absolute depth. While these models demonstrate strong performance on single image benchmarks and qualitatively consistent predictions in video, their effectiveness at preserving consistent spatial structure has been less thoroughly explored. Many potential real-world applications, such as handling video streams as input, rely on coherent three dimensional consistency in scenes. Further, anchoring relative depth predictions to a metric reference for a given scene is a key challenge for applying monocular depth models to real-world situations. We develop a novel evaluation protocol for monocular depth models using video sequences with moving camera positions to test the consistency of prediction across variation in viewpoint. We demonstrate this methodology over diverse, real-world video sequences where we are able to anchor depth model output to metric depth values using structure from motion. Our work demonstrates open challenges in the development of broadly applicable monocular depth foundation models, particularly with their ability to provide temporal consistency over long time frames. We also identify challenges in the straightforward adoption of structure-from-motion as a metric grounding tool for monocular depth estimation models.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出一套面向单目深度模型的评测协议，利用移动相机拍摄的视频序列并借助 structure from motion 将仿射不变深度锚定到度量深度，考察模型跨视角、长时段的空间与时间一致性。
